newsitem.title: USA: Whitewater prosecutor decides to stay on job.
newsitem.headline: Whitewater prosecutor decides to stay on job.

text.p: Whitewater prosecutor Kenneth Starr has decided to delay his departure as head of the investigation involving President and Mrs. Clinton, a Starr spokeswoman said on Friday.

Debbie Gershman of Starr's investigative office in Little Rock, Arkansas, declined to give further details but said they would be contained in a statement about to be released. An announcement by Pepperdine University on Monday that Starr would become dean of its law school had prompted speculation he was shifting jobs because he planned to file no charges against the Clintons.

Starr issued a statement clarifying his position after nearly a week of controversy over his expected imminent departure to become dean of Pepperdine University law school. This sparked speculation he was leaving because he had not developed enough evidence to bring charges against the Clintons, and some criticism of him personally.

"I have informed Pepperdine University that I intend to continue as independent counsel, and will assume no duties or responsibilities as dean at Pepperdine until the investigation and any resulting prosecutions of persons named in the order appointing me as independent counsel or high-level government officials have been substantially completed," Starr said in a statement released by his office.

His inquiry started as a probe of the Whitewater land deal involving the Clintons when the president was governor of Arkansas as well as the failure of an Arkansas savings and loan institution. It has since expanded to include a number of White House controversies including the firing of the travel office staff and the obtaining of FBI personal files.

"My commitment is to the American people and to the pursuit of the truth, and I will seek to fulfil that commitment to the best of my ability and for as long as it takes," Starr said. He expressed regret his decision to shift jobs "may have called that commitment into question."
